Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

how are you? phrase

also how are you doing?, greetings, how are things?, how are things with you?, how’s it going?, what’s doing?, how goes it?

classical

Traupman 15, 17–18
Traupman 330

Quid agis?

To two or more people: Quid agitis?, Ut valētis? (Traupman 17).

Other words

  • Ut valēs?

    also used · classical · Traupman 15, 17–18

  • Ut tē habēs?

    also used · classical · Traupman 15, 17–18

  • Quī valēs? — how are you?

    question: quī, the old ablative “how?”, with valēre, be well · also used · classical · Traupman 17: how are you?, quī valēs?

    Lewis & Short has quī “how?” in questions as classical; this question with valēs is Traupman’s.

  • Quō pactō rēs sē tibi habent? — how are things with you?

    question: “in what way do things hold themselves for you?” · also used · modern · Traupman 18: how are things with you?, quō pactō rēs sē tibi habent?

    Traupman’s phrase, made of classical parts (quō pactō, how; rēs sē habent, things stand); Lewis & Short does not quote it whole. Comedy asks Quid agitur? (Ter. Ad. 883).

  • Quō pactō tēcum agitur? — how are things with you?

    also used · modern · Traupman 146

    Agitur impersonal, “it goes”: compare bene agitur, things are going well.

  • Quid agitur? — how goes it? what’s doing?

    also used · classical · Plaut. Ps. 1.1.17: quid agitur? (Lewis & Short s.v. agō); Ter. Ad. 5.5.2: Syre noster, salvē, quid fit? quid agitur? (Lewis & Short s.v. noster); Traupman 305

    (vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut., Ter.)

  • Quid fit? — how goes it? what’s new?

    also used · classical · Ter. Ad. 883: Ō Syre noster, salvē: quid fit? quid agitur?; Traupman 330

Examples

  • Salvē, Baba! Ut valēs? — Bene, mī Theodōre.

    Hello, Baba! How are you? — Fine, my Theo.composed

See also I’m fine, not bad, what’s new?, goodbye.

SourcesLewis & Short: valeo

The example sentences marked “composed” are ours.

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 15, 17–18, 305, 330.
